summary: This Docker Compose file sets up two services: an ollama service that runs a large language model on port 11444 with persistent storage, and an app service that provides a development environment that depends on ollama and mounts the current directory for live code editing. The ollama service has commented-out GPU support that can be enabled if you have an NVIDIA GPU.

explanations.10: The port mapping forwards port 11444 on your computer to port 11434 inside the container where ollama listens — this lets you talk to ollama from outside Docker.
explanations.12: This creates a named storage volume called ollama_data and mounts it to /root/.ollama inside the container, so the LLM models persist even if the container restarts.
explanations.28: This mounts your current directory (.) on your computer into /workspaces/blog_analyzer inside the container, so any code changes you make locally instantly appear in the container.
explanations.29: The app service won't start until the ollama service is running, since the app likely needs to communicate with the ollama LLM.
explanations.32: The sleep infinity command keeps the container running indefinitely instead of exiting, allowing you to execute commands inside it.
